entities.summary: Edward Durell Stone was an American architect known for the formal, highly decorative buildings he designed in the 1950s and 1960s. His works include the Museum of Modern Art, in New York City; the Parliament House of Pakistan in Islamabad; the Museo de Arte de Ponce in Ponce, Puerto Rico; the United States Embassy in New Delhi, India; The Keller Center at the University of Chicago; the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C., the EcoTarium, formerly known as the New England Science Center in Worcester, Massachusetts; and the campus of Windham College in Putney, Vermont.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Edward Durell Stone's designs had a significant regional impact in North America, particularly in the development of modernist architecture and public buildings. His works can be seen as part of the broader cultural shift towards modernity in the post-war era.
